Why purchase your meat by the side?

Purchasing sides is the least expensive, most environmentally sound, and most humane way of purchasing meat. The animal is allowed to spend its entire life on the farm without being shipped to a slaughterhouse. Animals are slaughtered in a gentle and humane manner on the farm by local ODA-certified butchers. The cost for processing in this manner is significantly less, and we pass that savings on to you. 

 Estimated Final Price and Processed Weight:

$1260 for a half pork which results in around 125 pounds of meat, plus bones and organs.

How much product will I actually receive?

Since you are purchasing a live animal, it is difficult to give an exact amount until the animal is sacrificed. The actual weight of the product you receive (processed weight) will be approximately 70% of the hanging weight. Hanging weight (which the butcher will provide to the farm) is the weight of a carcass after slaughter and removal of organs, head, and hide. The processed weight is less because it accounts for the removal of bones, fat, and water lost during the dry-aging process. 

The take-home weight is also influenced by the choices of cuts you choose. Will you want bone-in or boneless roasts? Will you choose bone-in rib steaks or boneless ribeyes? Porterhouse and T-bone steaks have the bones, but they become Kansas City strip steaks and filet mignon without them. These decisions affect that total. You are also purchasing the fat and bones, and you should request those, or not, from the butcher’s cut sheet. 

How do I store the product?

The meat will be given to you frozen and it should be stored in the freezer. To estimate freezer space, plan on one paper grocery bag per 30lbs of product. 

What to expect when ordering by the side:

  1. First, purchase a "Side Deposit" in Full Farm CSA. Available to Guests, CSA Members and Herdshare members. This reserves the animal for the October 1st 2026 butcher date.
  2. Deck Family Farm continues to raise the animal to finishing weight.
  3. We will contact the customer the day after the processing with a final invoice based on the hanging weight. Invoice will be due at that time.
  4. The customer will be given access to the 4Star cut sheet to request how the meat should be portioned (ground, steaks, roasts, etc.)
  5. When final customer payment is received, 4-Star can release the order to the customer. 
  6. Pickup from 4Star for local orders (Eugene, Springfield, Corvallis and Salem). Delivery to Portland for $100.00.

Milled from the whole grain, grown in the Willamette Valley by Camas Country Mill. Teff is a fine grain - about the size of a poppy seed. Teff grows predominantly in Ethiopia and Eritrea, and thrives even in difficult climates. As such, it comprises the staple grain of their cuisines. The grain has a very mild, nutty flavor, and it packs a serious nutritional punch. Teff has an excellent balance of amino acids, and it is also high in protein, calcium, and iron. Ground into flour, teff is used to make the traditional bread, injera: a flat, pancake-like, fermented bread that complements the exotic spices found in the regional food. It can also be ground into flour to make an excellent gluten-free flour alternative, and can be used to make pie crusts, cookies, breads, and an assortment of other baked goods. Teff can also be eaten whole and steamed, boiled, or baked as a side dish or a main course.

Immunity:

Vitamin C in cauliflower can help protect the body from infection and reduce inflammation that can cause disease.

Brain health:

Cauliflower contains choline, a B vitamin that can help improve memory and learning by boosting cognitive function.

Bone health:

Cauliflower contains vitamin C, which helps produce collagen to protect bones and joints from inflammation, and vitamin K, which can help prevent bone loss.

Product: Dinner in a Box: Ground Lamb Bundle
Description:
Not sure what to make this week? Start here. This bundle is built around ground lamb from Deck Family Farm, paired with what's fresh right now: shiitake mushrooms, rainbow chard, beets, leeks, cabbage, potatoes, and pears. Add your yogurt and you've got a full week of dinners with no planning required.


Lamb & Mushroom Skillet Brown 1 lb ground lamb with sliced shiitakes and a leek. Add garlic and a big handful of rainbow chard. Season with salt, pepper, red pepper flake. Stir in raw yogurt off the heat. Serve over roasted potatoes. 25 minutes for a rich, clean meal.

Lamb-Stuffed Cabbage Rolls Blanch cabbage leaves, fill with seasoned ground lamb and sautéed onion, arrange in baking dish and simmer in a simple tomato broth. A classic — raw cream makes a great finish on top.

Pear & Lamb Flatbread Spread raw yogurt on flatbread, add crumbled cooked lamb, sliced pear and beet, caramelized leeks, and your cheese pick from this week's dairy. Heat in the oven to melt the cheese. 15 minutes to assemble.


TIPS: 1. Roast the potatoes while you prepare the rest. Add some beets for variety. 2. Brown all the lamb at once to simplify later meal prep. 3. Sauté all the leeks at once so you can add them easily later.

Product: Dinner in a Box: Pork Shoulder Roast
Description:
Ingredients: Pork shoulder, potatoes, salad turnips, spring onions, beets, lettuce, radish, farmer's cheese, bok choy, garlic, eggs

Recipe 1: 

Pulled Pork Tacos Warm tortillas, pile on pulled pork shoulder, sliced radish, shredded lettuce, and spring onion. Add a spoonful of farmer's cheese and a squeeze of lime. Done.

Recipe 2: 

Pork & Bok Choy Soup: Simmer pulled pork in broth with garlic, spring onion, and sliced crimini mushrooms. Stir in a spoonful of whole grain mustard. Add bok choy in the last few minutes until just wilted. Finish with sesame oil and a soft-boiled egg.

Recipe 3: 

Roasted Beet & Pork Bowl Roast beets until tender, slice thin. Arrange over torn lettuce with pulled pork, sliced radish, and spring onion. Top with crumbled farmer's cheese. Dress with olive oil, vinegar, and salt.

Recipe 4: 

Pork & Potato Hash: Dice pulled pork shoulder. Cook with cubed potatoes, sliced crimini mushrooms, salad turnips, and spring onions in butter until golden. Season with salt and pepper. Top with a fried egg.


From the Full Farm CSA shop:

  • Pork shoulder — 1 large (3–4 lbs, covers all four meals)
  • Crimini mushrooms — 1 lb
  • Potatoes — 4 medium
  • Salad turnips — 3 medium
  • Beets — 4 medium (red or yellow or chiogga)
  • Bok choy — 2 heads
  • Spring Mix Lettuce — 1 bag
  • Radish — 1 bunch
  • Spring onions — 1 bunch
  • Garlic — how much?
  • Farmer's cheese — 6 oz
  • Eggs — one dozen

Digestion: Zucchini is high in fiber and water, which can help with digestion and prevent constipation. The soluble fiber in zucchini can also benefit the healthy bacteria in your gut.

Weight management:Zucchini is low in calories and high in fiber and water, which can help you feel full and control your appetite.

Diabetes:Zucchini is rich in vitamin B6, which may help regulate blood glucose and protect against diabetes. It also contains magnesium and zinc, which can help break down sugar in the body.

Heart health:Zucchini is high in potassium, a heart-healthy mineral. High-fiber diets, like those that include zucchini, can also improve heart health.

Eye health:Zucchini contains beta-carotene, a carotenoid that the body can convert into vitamin A. Vitamin A helps with cell development in the eyes, which can improve vision and prevent age-related conditions like macular degeneration. Zucchini can also reduce swelling around the eyes.

Cancer prevention:Zucchini contains zeaxanthin and other compounds that may help prevent oxidative stress, which could reduce the risk of developing cancer.

Why purchase your meat by the side?

Purchasing sides is the least expensive, most environmentally sound, and most humane way of purchasing meat. The animal is allowed to spend its entire life on the farm without being shipped to a slaughterhouse. Animals are slaughtered in a gentle and humane manner on the farm by local ODA-certified butchers. The cost for processing in this manner is significantly less, and we pass that savings on to you. 

How much product will I actually receive?

Since you are purchasing a live animal, it is difficult to give an exact amount until the animal is sacrificed. The actual weight of the product you receive (processed weight) will be approximately 70% of the hanging weight. Hanging weight (which the butcher will provide to the farm) is the weight of a carcass after slaughter and removal of organs, head, and hide. The processed weight is less because it accounts for the removal of bones, fat, and water lost during the dry-aging process. 


The take-home weight is also influenced by the choices of cuts you choose. Will you want bone-in or boneless roasts?  These decisions affect that total. You are also purchasing the fat and bones, and you should request those, or not, from the butcher’s cut sheet.


How do I store the product?

The meat will be given to you frozen and it should be stored in the freezer. To estimate freezer space, plan on one paper grocery bag per 30lbs of product.
